newsitem.title: USA: FERC looking at Houston Industries merger.
newsitem.headline: FERC looking at Houston Industries merger.

text.p: Houston Industries Inc said Thursday the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has initiated an inquiry which could delay HI's completion of its pending merger with NorAm Energy Corp.

FERC Wednesday issued an order directing that NorAm's power marketing subsidiary make a filing setting forth its views on whether the pending merger requires FERC approval under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act. Alternatively, FERC invited NorAm to file an application seeking approval under Section 203.
Houston Industries said it and NorAm are studying the FERC order and will file a response in the near future.
It also said both companies remain convinced that no approval is required or warranted under Section 203, and that the application of FERC jurisdiction in these circumstances would be unprecedented.

The NorAm subsidiary, NorAm Energy Services Inc, holds FERC authorization to make market-based sales of electric power and energy. Under that authorization NES is required to notify FERC if there is a change in the characteristics relied on by FERC in granting that authorization.

In September 1996, NorAm Energy Services filed a notice with FERC advising that, following the merger, the marketer would become a subsidiary of a public utility -- Houston Industries' Houston Lighting & Power Co subsidiary.

But NorAm Energy Services sought to continue its status as a power marketer based on its compliance with FERC guidelines for utility power-marketer affiliates. That application remains pending at FERC.
Generally, Houston Industries noted, changes in a marketer's status are addressed by FERC administratively without hearing.

Under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act, a public utility subject to FERC's jurisdiction must obtain prior approval from FERC for a sale of its assets or a merger of its assets with those of another public utility.

By virtue of its authorization from FERC, NorAm Energy Services is subject to certain requirements as a public utility under the Federal Power Act, but Houston Lighting is not considered to be a "jurisdictional" public utility under that Act since it does not operate facilities that are engaged in the sale or transmission of electric power and energy in interstate commerce, Houston Industries' statement explained.

In its order initiating a jurisdictional inquiry, FERC concluded this situation raised an issue of whether FERC authorization under Section 203 is required for the merger transaction. FERC accordingly required NorAm to provide, within 30 days, its views as to why such approval is not required or, in the alternative, seek approval.
